propositions: A Jira issue's KEY changes when moved between projects while its numeric id is stable, and third-party move mechanisms can fail to update the moved_issue_key table so the old key stops resolving.
rebar bindings are keyed on the mutable jira_key across many methods, so a moved issue silently detaches and its local ticket is orphaned when the absence probe reads the stale key as gone.

The fix additively records the numeric jira_id on each binding and, on a key-lookup 404, re-asks by id and re-keys the binding to the current key while updating the reverse index in the same operation.

The approach is deliberately additive rather than re-keying the shared Cloud store, to avoid a large blast radius and remain correct under all three unresolved readings (200/301/404) of what a stale key returns.
Legacy bindings without a recorded id degrade to prior behavior with no migration, and the id fallback must not fire while the key still resolves so the happy path pays no extra cost.

The operator-attested question of what GET on a moved oldKey returns on DC 8.17.1 remains open because a real project move is not performable through pycontribs/jira 3.10.5, though live cells confirm id-resolution and that deletions are not masked.
